target_customer: Breeders, growers, seed banks and retailers in high-value plant markets, mainly legal California cannabis
problem: Conventional plant breeding is slow and trait selection is imprecise. Rev uses genome-wide selection, tissue culture and metabolite analytics to produce novel cultivars with valuable biochemicals.
business_model: Licensing of cultivars and IP to breeders and cultivators, plus fingerprinting and genomics services

founders.name: Bertrand Vick
founders.background_notes: From the company website team page.

founders.name: R.J. Cody Markelz
education: PhD, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the company website; the YC page lists only Vick.

technical_complexity.rationale: Genomic prediction, tissue culture and metabolite analytics for a crop with legal restrictions on research, run by an 8 person team, required real plant biology expertise.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary marker data and cultivars could be hard to copy, but cannabis varieties are easy to propagate and no patents assigned to Rev were found in a directory search.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found. Federal illegality kept large agricultural firms out of cannabis genetics at the time.

market_need_then: California legalized adult-use cannabis sales in 2018 and growers wanted consistent, high-potency, disease-resistant cultivars. Demo day coverage mentioned targeting Botrytis gray mold. No dated demand statistics were opened.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical; tagline A Biotechnology Company Making Better Plants

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself, no mascot or community found. The name is generic and resembles unrelated firms such as Revvity.

outcome_analysis: Rev Genomics was a small YC S17 plant biotech team led by an algae scientist, targeting cannabis breeding with genomic prediction. A 2019 public SNP dataset of 1,358 cultivars and 15 plus commercial strains were reported by one source, and the company still operates in Oakland. No verified funding, exit or failure evidence was found, so the outcome is unclear and growth appears slow.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights shows 1.62M total (possibly confused with another company), Bouncewatch shows a 120K seed on 2017-08-21 and a 2020-03-19 round with Merida Capital Holdings, amount unknown. Both are aggregators, so no round is recorded. Competitor list empty: no source dated near 2017 names rivals. Phylos Bioscience (Portland, cannabis genetics, 2016 GeekWire funding article) existed but I did not open the source, so it is not listed. Founding year 2016 per YC; other databases say 2015. Update: rounds now recorded from single databases. The 2017-08-21 seed of 120K and the 2020-03-19 round (amount unknown) rest on Bouncewatch only; the 2019-05 seed of about 1.5M rests on Seedtable only (a profile snippet cites a 2019 Form D with 1,495,360 sold of 2,000,000, not opened). Amounts and dates conflict across databases and CB Insights total of 1.62M is unreconciled. No press release found.
